approach: After the checks and replay, and before the verifier's disk gate, `verification_stage` calls a new `Athena::demonstration_records` (run/checks.rs). It takes the accepted plan's demonstrations (`closing.plans.last()`) that have a non-blank `fails_without` and a plain `cargo test ...` command, groups them by distinct command (each command runs once; the record lists every criterion that names it; at most 3 commands), and makes a scratch copy of the candidate with `verifier_snapshot` in `<job_dir>/revert`. Structure follows `take_baseline` (checks.rs:92-118): an inner Result fn, an outer fn that always calls `pin::remove_tree` and turns errors into 'not run' entries. In the copy every changed non-test file goes back to its base version; for a changed `.rs` file the candidate's `#[cfg(test)] mod` blocks AND its bodiless `#[cfg(test)] mod x;` declarations are carried over, and a file named by a carried declaration counts as test code and is kept. Added non-test files are removed; Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock stay. The command runs through `run_check` as `CheckKind::Test`; the outcome is classified from `exit_code` and `tests_ran`. The result is a 'not a check' `CheckResultView` with a `demonstration` sub-record, rendered under 'Checks Athena ran on this tree'. The stage runs real cargo only in production builds. In a build with `cfg(test)` or the `test-support` feature it runs only when a test has installed `demo_seam`; otherwise it adds nothing, so the fake-agent jobs in the CLI integration tests and the existing run/tests.rs jobs keep their text and speed. The verdict path (`check_runs`, `judge`) is untouched.

decisions.choice: The revert keeps the candidate's inline tests: for a changed .rs file, take the base text, drop the base's own `#[cfg(test)] mod` blocks and bodiless declarations, append the candidate's. Pure fn `verify::revert_keeping_tests(base, candidate) -> Option<RevertedFile>` (text plus the list of carried declarations).
decisions.reason: This repository keeps tests inline (about 93 source files have `mod tests`), so a whole-file revert would delete the new test and the record could only say 'ran no tests'. `syn` is already a dependency and code_health.rs:75-141 already finds test modules.

rejected.option: Whole-file revert, naming the file whose tests vanished
rejected.why: Leaves the common case without a failing run, the problem this job removes. Kept only as the fallback for a file that does not parse.

rejected.option: Hunk-level revert
rejected.why: Needs a diff/patch engine and breaks on hunks that cross the test-module boundary.

rejected.option: A `revert` field on Demonstration or planner prompt changes
rejected.why: Out of scope; the prompts have no token headroom.

decisions.choice: Answer finding 3 (declared test modules): `code_health::test_module_ranges` returns both bodied `#[cfg(test)] mod x { .. }` ranges and bodiless `#[cfg(test)] mod x;` declaration ranges (new `test_decls` field on `Scan`, set in `visit_item_mod` where `content` is None; `measure_source` and `test_ranges` are not changed). `revert_keeping_tests` carries both kinds over. The declared module's file is resolved from the parent path (`dir/x.rs` or `dir/x/mod.rs`; for a parent that is not lib.rs/main.rs/mod.rs also `dir/<parent stem>/x.rs`) and, when it is among the changed files, is kept as test code even if its name is not a test-file name. If a declared file cannot be found among the changed files nothing is changed for it. Any file reverted or removed while the candidate holds `#[cfg(test)]` code in it goes in `tests_removed`, and the brief names it.
decisions.reason: The repository declares test modules without a body (lib.rs:108-109, gh/mod.rs:109-110, athena-gate/src/lib.rs:387-388). Without carrying the declaration, a new `*_tests.rs` file would be kept but never compiled, and the run would say 'ran no tests' without naming it.

rejected.option: Only list the orphaned file in tests_removed
rejected.why: The common case (fix plus a new test file) would still show no failing run.

rejected.option: Change `Scan::test_ranges` to include bodiless modules
rejected.why: It feeds the file-length measure; its meaning must not change.

decisions.choice: Fallbacks stay visible: a changed .rs file that does not parse (base or candidate), or an added non-test file holding `#[cfg(test)]` code, is reverted whole or removed and its path goes in `tests_removed`; the brief prints 'tests inside these files were removed with the revert: <paths>'.
decisions.reason: If a test is removed the verifier must be told which file, not just 'ran no tests'. An added file with inline tests cannot stay because the `mod x;` line in its parent is reverted.

rejected.option: Keep an added .rs file that has tests
rejected.why: Its declaring `mod` line is reverted, so it would never be compiled.

decisions.choice: Keep Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock as the candidate has them; revert every other changed non-test file.
decisions.reason: The checks run with `--locked`; reverting a manifest that adds a dev-dependency the new test needs would fail on resolution, not on the missing fix.

rejected.option: Revert manifests too
rejected.why: Gives failures that are not 'the test fails without the fix'.

decisions.choice: Run the demonstration as `CheckKind::Test`; classify from `CheckRun.exit_code` and `CheckRun.tests_ran` (counted by `run_check` on the full output, checks.rs:501), never from the clipped tail. Exit 0 with tests_ran > 0 = 'passed without the fix: the revert did not make the test fail'; exit 0 with 0 tests = 'ran no tests'; non-zero = 'the named test command failed without the fix (exit N)' plus ': the test did not compile' if the output holds 'could not compile' or 'error[E'; no exit code = 'did not finish'.
decisions.reason: A filtered `cargo test -p x name` prints one summary per binary and the tail (TAIL_BYTES 4096, checks.rs:26) can hold only trailing '0 passed' lines. A compile error without the fix is a genuine failing run when the test calls a new function, so the sentence states the cause neutrally.

rejected.option: CheckKind::Command and count_tests on the tail
rejected.why: Misreads a run that did execute the test as 'ran no tests'.

rejected.option: Label a build failure 'not a test failure'
rejected.why: Invites the verifier to treat the criterion as unshown.

decisions.choice: Only a plain `cargo test ...` command runs (backticks stripped, split on whitespace; a shell metacharacter or quote gives 'not run: not a plain cargo test command'). Demonstrations are grouped by identical command: each distinct command runs once, and its single entry (`fails-without-<first criterion>`) lists every criterion that names it. At most 3 distinct commands run; the rest are named as not run.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 4: planners reuse `cargo test --locked` (fake.rs:366, lifecycle.rs:2648), and one full suite run on one reverted tree is enough. It is the form the verifier grant allows and admission checks; the cap bounds wall time, each run bounded by `check_timeout_s`.

rejected.option: One run per criterion
rejected.why: Runs the same full suite up to 3 times on the same tree.

rejected.option: Run any command the verifier grant allows
rejected.why: Needs the full policy parser; `cargo build` or `git` cannot usefully fail without the fix.

decisions.choice: The record is a `CheckResultView` with command 'not a check', `passed: true`, plus an optional `demonstration` sub-record (`DemonstrationRunView`: criteria, command, reverted files, tests_removed files, exit code, output tail), rendered in its own branch in briefs.rs that never prints passed/failed for it. Nothing enters `check_runs`, `Verification.checks` or `judge`.
decisions.reason: Follows `ci-result`, `producer-report-gaps` and `criteria-left-to-athena-checks` (verification.rs:88-127). A failing demonstration cannot fail the verdict.

rejected.option: Push a CheckRun into check_runs
rejected.why: A failing run would fail the verdict and enter the records.

rejected.option: Free text in `detail`
rejected.why: The renderer would print passed/failed beside a 'failing' run and the tail would not be fenced as data.

decisions.choice: Reuse `Athena::verifier_snapshot` (verification.rs:405) for the scratch copy under `<job_dir>/revert`, `athena_agent::env::build` with Side::Verify (as `baseline_checks`, checks.rs:135-146) and `run_check`. Share `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.
decisions.reason: The copy has the candidate work tree and base tool configuration exactly as the checks saw them; `run_check` brings the timeout, kill switch, redaction and process registration; the shared target reuses third-party builds. The candidate commit, the job repository and the verifier's snapshot are never written.

rejected.option: Revert inside the verifier's snapshot and restore
rejected.why: A crash would leave the prepared tree dirty.

rejected.option: A separate CARGO_TARGET_DIR
rejected.why: A cold build of every dependency; disk is the scarce resource.

decisions.choice: Run the stage before `verifier_environment_problem`; skip it when `self.nested.is_some()`; never let it fail the job (every problem becomes a 'not run: <reason>' entry).
decisions.reason: The disk gate then measures the space left after the extra build, and a scratch fault must not reject correct work.

rejected.option: Run inside check_and_verify with the checks
rejected.why: That stage does not hold the accepted plan yet.

In a build with that cfg, `demonstration_records` returns no entries unless a mapper is installed; in a production build (neither cfg) it always runs real cargo. The shared fake planner (fake.rs:353-372, `cargo test --locked` with a fails_without for every criterion) is NOT changed.

With nothing installed the verifier brief text those tests read (job_plan.rs:345-348) and their running time are unchanged. The mapper maps only the program, so the revert, scratch copy, process and classification are production code.

rejected.why: Not compiled into the CLI integration tests, so they would run real cargo.

risks.risk: A test helper or `#[cfg(test)]` item outside a `mod`, a test module nested inside a non-test item, or a `#[path]` declaration is not carried over, so the reverted copy may not compile.
risks.mitigation: A non-zero exit with a compile error is reported as 'failed without the fix: the test did not compile (exit N)' with the reverted files listed. Only top-level bodied modules and bodiless `mod x;` declarations are swapped; the repository convention (`mod tests { .. }`, `#[cfg(test)] mod x;`) is covered by unit tests.

risks.mitigation: Those paths are listed in `tests_removed` and the brief says so; a zero-test run stays 'ran no tests', never read as a failing run.

risks.risk: In production the stage adds cold-build wall time and disk use before the verifier (an estimate, not measured: minutes per distinct command).
risks.mitigation: Cap of 3 distinct commands, each bounded by `check_timeout_s`; the target directory is shared with the checks; the copy is removed afterwards; the disk gate runs after the runs.

risks.risk: Failing to make or remove the scratch copy could fail the job or leak a directory.
risks.mitigation: Outer/inner structure as in `take_baseline`: `remove_tree` always runs and errors become 'not run: <reason>' entries; a kill-switch stop comes through `run_check` as a note.

risks.risk: The command comes from a model-written plan and runs on the candidate's code.
risks.mitigation: Only `cargo test` with no shell metacharacters or quotes runs, with the checks' scrubbed environment (`env_clear` in `run_check`), in a copy that holds the candidate only; admission already checked the command against the verifier grant.

risks.risk: Real cargo is exercised only in production, so the real `cargo test` form is covered by the parse and classification unit tests, not by an end-to-end run; the job-level tests map `cargo test` to `sh -c`.
risks.mitigation: The mapper changes only the program; the revert, scratch copy, process, classification and rendering are production code. The recorded checks run `cargo test --locked` on the real tree.

risks.risk: The third job-level test needs a base repo with `src/notes.rs` and a producer edit other than the README.
risks.mitigation: The test wraps the script as `run_planned_behavior` wraps the reader (tests.rs:640-648), and the plan lists the extra file. If the scope check objects, fall back to a checks.rs-level test that calls the inner revert function on a real `verifier_snapshot`; `revert_keeping_tests` has pure unit tests either way.

risks.risk: Non-test line counts of briefs.rs (177 KB) and verify.rs (70 KB) may approach the 2000-line file check (code_health.rs:36).
risks.mitigation: Reuse `Scan` through a thin fn; keep the briefs.rs rendering to one helper; the producer counts non-test lines before finishing.

risks.risk: The scope check flags code_health.rs as outside the listed deliverables.
risks.mitigation: The change description names it as reuse of the single definition of a test module, a thin addition that leaves `measure_source` unchanged.

demonstrations.seam: Same entry point, fixtures and `demo_seam` as criterion 1 (step 4). `verify::demonstration_view` is real code (step 3); no double contains it.

demonstrations.method: Rendering tests in briefs.rs call `verifier_brief_with_plan` with `VerifierInputs.checks` holding (a) an entry with a `demonstration` sub-record (criteria [1, 2], command `cargo test --locked demo`, exit code 101, reverted files, a `tests_removed` file, a multi-line tail containing a ``` fence) and (b) one with exit code 0; a third test checks an old-style entry (`..Default::default()`) renders exactly as before.
demonstrations.observes: Under '## Checks Athena ran on this tree' the text has the command in backticks, 'exit code 101', the result sentence, the criteria, the reverted files, the 'tests inside these files were removed with the revert' line, and the clipped tail in a fenced block (inner fence neutralised by `clip_log_tail`). The entry prints neither 'passed' nor 'failed' as its own status. The existing briefs.rs tests (the full literal ~3273 and ~3445) still pass.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the rendering branch the exit code and tail are absent and the assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `athena_context::briefs::verifier_brief_with_plan` (exists, ~briefs.rs:1075). No double: the test builds the input struct directly. `DemonstrationRunView` and the `demonstration` field are added by step 1.

demonstrations.method: Content check of the diff plus the criterion 1 test, which asserts that after the run `<job_dir>/revert` is gone and the candidate commit still holds README.md as the candidate wrote it. A unit test of the outer fn with an inner error (the scratch directory cannot be made) shows 'not run' and no leftover directory.
demonstrations.command: git diff -- crates/athena-core/src/run/checks.rs crates/athena-core/src/run/verification.rs && cargo test -p athena-core a_planned_fails_without_demonstration_is_run_on_a_reverted_copy_and_shown_to_the_verifier
demonstrations.observes: The only writes are inside the directory created by `verifier_snapshot(&job_dir.join("revert"), ..)`; `pin::remove_tree` runs in the outer function on every path (as in `take_baseline`); no git write runs against the job repository or the candidate.

demonstrations.method: Content check of the diff plus the criterion 1 and 2 tests, which land the job with a failing demonstration (exit 1) and a passing one (exit 0).
demonstrations.observes: The entries are pushed only to `inputs.checks` with `command: "not a check"`, `passed: true`; not to `check_runs`, `Verification.checks` or `VerdictInputs.checks`; `judge` is not edited. The criterion 1 job lands although the demonstration exits 1.

demonstrations.method: The recorded Athena checks on the final tree. The producer also runs `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` and `cargo test -p athena-cli` as no-regression checks. The new unit tests include `revert_keeping_tests` cases: fix plus inline `mod tests`; a base with its own old test module (replaced); no test module; an unparsable file (None, whole-file fallback); a candidate with a bodiless `#[cfg(test)] mod x_tests;` whose file is kept and whose declaration is carried over; a declared module with a non-test file name that is kept; an added file with inline tests (listed in tests_removed); the `is_test_path` forms. A job-level test `a_planned_job_without_a_demo_runner_records_no_demonstration` (no mapper installed, plan with fails_without, command `cargo test --locked`) lands and its verifier prompt has no `fails-without` entry.
demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
demonstrations.observes: All three pass; the existing tests.rs:861 job, which uses `behavior_plan`, and the athena-cli integration tests that use the fake planner behave as before.
demonstrations.fails_without: A compile error, a clippy warning or a failing test fails the matching check; a `revert_keeping_tests` that dropped the candidate's inline module or declaration fails its unit test; a stage that ran real cargo with no mapper would make `a_planned_job_without_a_demo_runner_records_no_demonstration` find an entry and fail.
demonstrations.seam: Whole workspace, no double. The `demonstration` field has a Default; the one full literal in briefs.rs (~3273) is updated in step 1. The no-mapper test uses existing fixtures and installs nothing.

demonstrations.observes: Under '## [Unreleased]' / '### Added' an entry says the verifier now sees Athena's recorded 'fails without the fix' run: Athena reverts the fix in a scratch copy of the candidate (keeping tests, including inline and declared test modules), runs the named test once per distinct command, and shows command, exit code and output tail under 'Checks Athena ran on this tree'. It names the root cause: the verifier gets no producer report and cannot change files.

open_questions: User: Should a demonstration whose command is not a plain `cargo test` (for example `cargo build` or a command with shell syntax) only be recorded as 'not run', as planned, or should the runner support more command forms?
